pages.about.description.en: Who runs this site, why it is built the way it is, and how it is kept current. Independent, unofficial, and not affiliated with any government.

pages.about.body[0].text.en: This site is run by one person in Brampton, Ontario. It is independent. It is not a government site, it is not affiliated with any government, and nothing on it is endorsed or approved by one.

pages.about.body[1].text.en: It exists because the pieces of this story are all published somewhere and almost nobody assembles them. The federal pages have the instruments and no locality. The municipal hubs have the local framing and no data of their own. The academic mapping reaches the neighbourhood and stops before saying what anyone should do. A reader is expected to join those up themselves, and almost nobody does. This site is the join.

pages.about.body[3].text.en: Every fact is written once and stored once, at three depths, in one record. The doors change which depth you read, not which document you are in. That is not a design flourish; it is the only arrangement under which one person can keep four audiences current, and it is why this can be free.

pages.about.body[4].text.en: The seasons on the People door work the same way. They filter which steps you see. They never change a fact, because a fact does not change with the reader's age.

pages.about.body[6].text.en: One pass every Monday morning through the Prime Minister's page, Finance Canada, the Canada Gazette Part II, the CBSA customs notices and a news sweep. Records that changed are updated, their checked dates are bumped, and the site rebuilds itself. On a normal week that is about forty minutes. In the week a major instrument lands it is about two hours.

pages.about.body[7].text.en: The site works out its own staleness and displays it. If a record has not been rechecked it says so on the record. If the whole file has gone unchecked, a notice appears before anything else. None of that is typed in by hand, which is the point: a promise to stay current is only worth what the mechanism behind it is worth.

pages.about.body[8].text.en: If you cannot rely on being online

pages.about.body[11].text.en: The same person also builds a small family of consumer safety tools under the Guardian name. Those are separate work, separately named, and this site carries none of it and earns nothing from it. The connection worth stating is the discipline rather than the brand: report gaps as gaps, refuse rather than guess, and never claim a clean result you did not earn.

pages.about.body[13].text.en: This is a bounded personal project rather than an institution. It runs for the duration of this disruption and is then archived honestly, or it is deliberately handed to a body that can carry it. The failure it is designed to avoid is the third path, where a site drifts, nobody says it is over, and it sits there being quietly wrong.

pages.about.body[14].text.en: Corrections and questions go to dasoftworks@gmail.com. It is read by a person, and corrections are welcome and acted on.

pages.promise.stamp.en: Version 1.0, published 24 August 2026. This page has a stable address and is versioned, so it can be cited in a decision about whether to link here.

pages.promise.description.en: What this site commits to: it takes no money, collects nothing about you, requests nothing from any other host, corrects itself in public, and says so within thirty days if it stops being maintained.

pages.promise.body[0].text.en: If you are deciding whether to put a link to this on a page you are accountable for, this is what you are agreeing to and what you are not.

pages.promise.body[2].text.en: No advertising. No sponsorship. No donations. No paid tier. No affiliate links. No sponsored content. No paywall. No lead generation, and no consulting funnel pointed at anyone who reads this.

pages.promise.body[3].text.en: That is spelled out rather than summarised as free, because free is compatible with all of it. It is also not generosity. Almost every legal footing this site stands on depends on it being non-commercial, and those footings shift together the moment money enters. Keeping it unfunded is the cheapest way to keep it defensible, which makes the commitment self-interested and therefore more reliable than one made out of goodwill.

pages.promise.body[4].text.en: It will never collect anything about you

pages.promise.body[5].text.en: No accounts. No login. No tracking. No analytics that identify a reader. No email address required to read anything. No third-party requests of any kind, which includes fonts: this page loads nothing from anywhere else, so reading it discloses your address to nobody.

pages.promise.body[6].text.en: It tells you how old it is

pages.promise.body[7].text.en: Every record shows the date it was last checked against its original source, and the site works out its own staleness rather than being told. This is a promise about the mechanism, not the outcome. The site will not always be current. It will always tell you whether it is.

pages.promise.body[8].text.en: It will tell you when it stops

pages.promise.body[9].text.en: If this site is no longer being maintained, a notice will appear at the top of every page within thirty days saying so and giving the date of the last check. The pages will be archived in place, still readable and clearly marked historical. They will not be silently left looking current, and they will not vanish and break your link. Anyone who has linked here and said so will be told directly beforehand.

pages.promise.body[10].text.en: It wants nothing from you in return

pages.promise.body[11].text.en: Link to it, embed it, quote it, print it and hand it to somebody, reproduce any of it with attribution. There will be no request for a logo, a co-brand, a press release or a reciprocal link. Roughly a dozen Ontario municipalities are each separately maintaining a near-identical list of programme links. The purpose here is to carry some of that duplicated effort, not to compete with the pages carrying it now.

pages.promise.body[13].text.en: Mistakes will happen. When one is found it is fixed quickly and recorded in the corrections log, showing what was wrong, what it changed to, and when.

pages.promise.body[15].text.en: It is legal and practical information, not legal advice. It is written for classes of reader rather than for anybody's particular situation.

pages.promise.body[16].text.en: It is not customs brokerage. It will never tell a named business which code to declare its goods under. The importer of record is responsible for their own declaration, and a licensed broker or an advance ruling is the authoritative route.

pages.promise.body[17].text.en: It is not financial advice. Where a question is genuinely about your own money and timing, this site names the question and names who answers it rather than offering a softer version of an answer it is not qualified to give.

pages.promise.body[18].text.en: Every substantive claim links to the document it came from. Where this site and the original disagree, the original is right and this site is wrong, and it would like to be told.

shocks.US_S338_2026-08.title.en: United States 50 percent tariffs on selected Canadian goods

shocks.US_S338_2026-08.plain.en: The United States has put a 50 percent tax on about one twentieth of what Canada sells them. Most trade is not on this list. It does cover hockey equipment, furniture, clothing, wine and beer, dairy, cement, plywood, circuit boards and some vehicles. If your workplace ships any of those south, this is the week to ask your employer what it means for orders.

shocks.US_S338_2026-08.operator.en: Effective 12:01am on 19 August 2026 across 554 tariff subheadings in three proclamations. The United States importer of record pays the duty, so the pressure arrives as cancelled orders and price renegotiation rather than as a bill to you. Qualifying under CUSMA does not exempt these lines, which catches most people out. Stop quoting a US landed cost without it, and check your Incoterms to confirm who actually carries the duty.

shocks.US_S338_2026-08.policy.en: First use in history of Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930, which permits up to 50 percent against a country found to have discriminated against United States commerce, requires no investigation and carries no expiry. Three proclamations: 52 subheadings covering dairy and agriculture, 439 covering motor vehicles and diverse manufactured and agricultural goods, and 63 covering alcohol, wood, paper and hockey equipment. Chapter 99 headings 9903.03.12 to 9903.03.14 carry the 50 percent rate; 9903.03.15 and 9903.03.16 list carve-outs at zero. Goods already under Section 232 are generally excluded. Legal challenge is widely expected given the statute has no judicial precedent.

shocks.US_S338_2026-08.facts[2].value.en: Roughly 5 percent of Canadian goods exports to the US

shocks.CA_RETAL_2026-09.plain.en: Canada is answering with its own taxes on American goods, starting Tuesday 8 September, the day after Labour Day. The list was published 25 August: steel, dairy, appliances, farm equipment, paper, electronics and more, covering 27.6 billion dollars of what Canada buys from the US. Each product gets matched to whatever rate the US is charging on the equivalent Canadian good, so some items carry 15 percent, some 25, some 50.

shocks.CA_RETAL_2026-09.operator.en: The product list and rate schedule were published 25 August 2026 and updated 26 August, covering 27.6 billion dollars of US imports at 15, 25 or 50 percent depending on the good, mirroring the US rate on the matching line. If you import from the United States, 8 September is the date that changes your landed cost, not 19 August. Named sectors are steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics. Check your own HS codes against the published list now rather than waiting for the formal surtax order and CBSA customs notice, which will formalize what has already been announced.

shocks.CA_RETAL_2026-09.policy.en: Announced by the Prime Minister on 22 August 2026 following suspension of negotiations. The Department of Finance published the product list and rate structure on 25 August 2026, updated 26 August, setting three tariff rates of 15, 25 and 50 percent, with each product's rate matching what the United States charges on the equivalent Canadian good, covering 27.6 billion dollars of US imports. The formal surtax order in Canada Gazette Part II and the CBSA customs notice giving declaration detail were not yet located as of this check on 27 August 2026 and should still be confirmed against the Department of Finance list in the meantime.

shocks.CA_RETAL_2026-09.facts[2].value.en: Product list and rates published 25 August 2026, updated 26 August (27.6 billion dollars of US imports)

shocks.CA_RETAL_2026-09.facts[3].value.en: 15, 25 or 50 percent, matching the US rate line for line

shocks.CA_SUPPORT_2026-08.title.en: Federal support package for affected workers and businesses

shocks.CA_SUPPORT_2026-08.plain.en: The federal government has now published exactly what it is doing to help workers and businesses hurt by these tariffs: an extra 7.5 billion dollars announced 25 August, on top of nearly 25 billion dollars already put into support programs over the past year and a half. It covers loans and grants for affected businesses, extra help for large employers under strain, and better Employment Insurance for people who are laid off or have their hours cut. If your hours are cut, ask your employer about Work-Sharing and the expanded EI measures, since those are the two programs built to keep people on payroll or afloat between jobs.

shocks.CA_SUPPORT_2026-08.operator.en: Announced 25 August 2026 as 7.5 billion dollars in new and enhanced measures, layered on nearly 25 billion dollars the government says it has delivered over the prior 18 months. The five pieces: the Regional Tariff Response Initiative (1.5 billion, higher per-SME funding caps), the BDC Pivot to Grow program (500 million in new working-capital loans of 250,000 to 5 million dollars), the Canada Strong Diversification Fund (2 billion, a new Strategic Response Fund stream), Rapid Response Supports for Workers and Employers (3.5 billion, including waived EI waiting periods, expanded benefits and a Workforce Retention and Retraining Program), and expanded flexibility on the existing 10 billion dollar Large Enterprise Tariff Loan Facility (up to 36 months of liquidity support, 15-year maximum terms). Application windows for the newer pieces are still opening; have your last two years of financials, your US revenue concentration and your affected headcount ready.

shocks.CA_SUPPORT_2026-08.policy.en: Announced 25 August 2026 as 7.5 billion dollars in new and enhanced measures, on top of nearly 25 billion dollars in supports the government says it has delivered over the prior 18 months, including the earlier 1 billion dollar Business Development Bank of Canada program and 500 million dollars in additional Regional Tariff Response Initiative funding announced in May 2026, delivered through the regional development agencies. Delivery agents and full eligibility criteria for each new stream were still being rolled out as of this check on 27 August 2026. Earlier working notes in this project carried unsourced figures for a national support envelope; those should be discarded in favour of this one.

shocks.CA_SUPPORT_2026-08.facts[2].value.en: Published 25 Aug 2026: Regional Tariff Response Initiative (1.5B), BDC Pivot to Grow (500M), Canada Strong Diversification Fund (2B), Rapid Response Supports for Workers and Employers (3.5B), and expanded flexibility on the existing 10B Large Enterprise Tariff Loan Facility

shocks.CA_STEEL_ALU_2025.title.en: Canadian surtax on United States steel and aluminum

shocks.CA_STEEL_ALU_2025.plain.en: Canada has had its own tax on American steel and aluminum since March 2025, well before this month. It is 25 percent, it is still in place, and it is part of why building materials have been getting more expensive. From 8 September 2026 that charge doubles to 50 percent.

shocks.CA_STEEL_ALU_2025.operator.en: A 25 percent surtax on US-origin steel and aluminum, in force since 13 March 2025 and separate from anything happening in September. It already sits in your landed cost. The schedule of covered goods was replaced on 1 September 2025, so a list you saved before that date is out of date. A remission framework exists for steel derivative goods, so if you are paying surtax on inputs with no Canadian substitute, that is worth raising with your broker. Goods marked as originating in Puerto Rico, Guam, the Northern Mariana Islands, American Samoa or the US Virgin Islands are outside the order. Finance Canada's published counter-tariff list confirms that steel and aluminum goods already carrying the 25 percent surtax move to 50 percent on 8 September 2026, under this same order rather than a new one. Price anything landing on or after that date at the higher rate, and check your classifications against the published list rather than against a schedule you saved earlier.

shocks.CA_STEEL_ALU_2025.policy.en: United States Surtax Order (Steel and Aluminum 2025), SOR/2025-95, registered 12 March 2025 and effective 13 March 2025, imposing 25 percent of the value for duty on US-origin goods in the listed classifications. Amended 27 March 2025, 8 April 2025, and 1 September 2025, the last of which replaced Schedule 1 with Schedule 2. Not repealed. Note that the consolidated text on the Justice Laws site is current only to 17 June 2026, so an amendment made after that date would not yet appear there and should be checked against the CBSA customs notices. Finance Canada's complete list of US products subject to counter-tariffs, published 25 August 2026 and updated 26 August, increases the rate on the steel and aluminum goods already covered by this order from 25 to 50 percent effective 8 September 2026. The increase runs under this order, SOR/2025-95, rather than a separate instrument.

shocks.CA_STEEL_ALU_2025.facts[3].value.en: Steel Derivative Goods Surtax Remission Order exists

shocks.CA_CABINETS_2026-07.title.en: Global safeguard on imported cabinets and vanities

shocks.CA_CABINETS_2026-07.plain.en: Kitchen cabinets and bathroom vanities brought into Canada from most countries carry an extra 25 percent charge. Cabinets made in Canada, the United States or Mexico are not affected. This has nothing to do with the argument with the United States, and it is temporary while a tribunal decides whether to make it permanent.

shocks.CA_CABINETS_2026-07.operator.en: A provisional safeguard surtax of 25 percent of the value for duty on certain wood cabinets and vanities and their subassemblies, including flat-pack, in force from 31 July 2026 for up to 200 days. It does not apply to goods originating in Canada, the United States, Mexico, Chile, Israel or another CIFTA beneficiary, or in developing countries. If you are sourcing cabinets from the United States or Mexico this does not touch your cost. If you are sourcing from elsewhere in Asia or Europe it very likely does, and it is a live line in a renovation quote alongside the steel and aluminum surtax. Classification of a subassembly is not obvious here, so confirm it with your broker rather than assuming.

shocks.CA_CABINETS_2026-07.policy.en: Certain Wood Cabinet and Vanity Goods Surtax Order, effective 31 July 2026, imposing 25 percent of the value for duty as a provisional safeguard for a period of up to 200 days while the Canadian International Trade Tribunal conducts a global safeguard inquiry. The Tribunal inquiry is expected to conclude by 15 January 2027 and the provisional measure ceases if no injury to domestic producers is found. The exclusions follow Canada's trade obligations rather than being discretionary, which is why the United States and Mexico are outside it. This is a domestic trade remedy and not a counter-measure, and treating it as part of the United States dispute misreads it.

shocks.TALKS_SUSPENDED_2026-08.plain.en: Canada walked away from a deal rather than sign one it judged bad. That means there is no quick fix coming and no date to wait for. Plan on this lasting.

shocks.TALKS_SUSPENDED_2026-08.operator.en: There is no near-term settlement to hold out for, so treat the current cost structure as the working assumption for at least the next two quarters rather than as a temporary spike to absorb. That changes the calculation on repricing, on qualifying an alternate supplier, and on whether to renew a US-dependent contract at current terms.

shocks.TALKS_SUSPENDED_2026-08.policy.en: Negotiations suspended on the evening of 21 August 2026 and negotiators recalled to Ottawa, with the Prime Minister citing terms described as uneconomic and unfair and demands that would have constrained Canada's ability to conclude other trade agreements. Sovereignty, protection of the French language and culture were stated as never having been on the table. The stated alternative track is domestic building and diversification, including more than twenty trade and security agreements signed in the past year, tariff-free access to 1.5 billion consumers with an intent to double that within six months through ASEAN and India, and European Union discussions opening this autumn.

actions.ACT_ASK_EMPLOYER_EXPOSURE.text.en: Ask your employer directly whether your plant or site ships to the United States, and whether any of it is on the 50 percent list.

actions.ACT_ASK_EMPLOYER_EXPOSURE.note.en: Most Canadian trade is not affected. Knowing which side of that line your workplace sits on is the single most useful thing you can find out.

actions.ACT_ASK_WORK_SHARING.text.en: If your hours are already being cut, ask whether your employer is applying for Work-Sharing.

actions.ACT_ASK_WORK_SHARING.note.en: Work-Sharing keeps people on payroll at reduced hours instead of laying them off, and it has to be applied for by the employer, not by you.

actions.ACT_READ_STANDARDS_EARLY.text.en: Find out now what your province's rules are on reduced hours and temporary layoff.

actions.ACT_READ_STANDARDS_EARLY.note.en: The thresholds differ by province and they matter. Reading them while calm is a different experience from reading them the week hours are cut.

actions.ACT_PRICES_MOVE_SEPTEMBER.text.en: Expect some prices to move in September, not August, and mostly on American-made goods.

actions.ACT_PRICES_MOVE_SEPTEMBER.note.en: The Canadian counter-tariffs are what touch shop prices here. They start 8 September and the product list is not published yet.

actions.ACT_WAIT_FOR_THE_GAZETTE.text.en: Treat any specific claim about which products are affected as unconfirmed until the list is published in the Canada Gazette.

actions.ACT_WAIT_FOR_THE_GAZETTE.note.en: News explains why something is happening. The Gazette and the CBSA customs notice are what actually happened.

actions.ACT_CHOOSE_A_DIRECTION.text.en: Before committing to a programme or a first job, look at which industries near you are exposed and which are not.

actions.ACT_CHOOSE_A_DIRECTION.note.en: This is the one season where the useful response is about direction rather than defence. Nothing here is urgent, and none of it should change a decision you have already made well.

actions.ACT_ASK_AT_OFFER_STAGE.text.en: If you have an offer from a company that exports, ask what share of its sales go to the United States.

actions.ACT_ASK_AT_OFFER_STAGE.note.en: It is a fair question at offer stage and the answer tells you more about the next two years than the job title does. A diversified customer base is a different position from selling almost entirely south.

actions.ACT_TIMING_RISK_NOT_TARIFFS.text.en: If you are within a few years of turning savings into income, the question worth raising is timing risk, not tariffs.

actions.ACT_TIMING_RISK_NOT_TARIFFS.note.en: This reaches you through currency and market movement rather than through employment, and it lands on the conversion moment rather than the accumulation years. The answer depends entirely on your own circumstances, so this page names the question rather than answering it.

actions.ACT_ANNOUNCED_IS_NOT_IN_FORCE.te.en: Announced is not in force. Several measures being discussed this month do not exist as instruments yet.

actions.ACT_ANNOUNCED_IS_NOT_IN_FORCE.no.en: This page marks which is which for exactly that reason. The status on each card above is the thing to read before acting on anything.

actions.ACT_FIXED_INCOME_WATCH_CANADA.te.en: On a fixed income the exposure is prices rather than employment, so the list to watch is the Canadian one.

actions.ACT_FIXED_INCOME_WATCH_CANADA.no.en: Counter-measures raise the cost of goods coming in from the United States, which is what reaches a shopping basket. The measures already in force apply to what Canada sells outward and mostly do not.

actions.ACT_WAIT_ON_A_BIG_PURCHASE.text.en: If you were planning to replace something imported and expensive this autumn, the early September list is worth waiting to read.

actions.ACT_WAIT_ON_A_BIG_PURCHASE.note.en: Two weeks of patience costs nothing while the list is unpublished. This is not a suggestion to buy early, which would be acting on a guess about a document that does not exist yet.

actions.ACT_ANSWER_THE_CHILDREN.text.en: If children in the house are picking up on the worry, the plain version is that this affects some workplaces and not most, and that nobody has lost anything yet.

actions.ACT_ANSWER_THE_CHILDREN.note.en: Children generally handle a specific and honest answer better than an atmosphere with no answer in it.

actions.ACT_HOURS_CUT_FIRST_CALLS.text.en: If household hours are reduced, the first calls are to Employment Insurance and to whoever holds your largest fixed payment, in that order.

actions.ACT_HOURS_CUT_FIRST_CALLS.note.en: Lenders and utilities have hardship processes that work considerably better when contacted before a payment is missed rather than after.

actions.ACT_TARIFF_CLAUSE_IN_QUOTES.text.en: Put a tariff clause in every open quote and every contract you are about to sign.

actions.ACT_TARIFF_CLAUSE_IN_QUOTES.note.en: A quote issued today without one is a quote you may have to honour at a cost you cannot yet calculate.

actions.ACT_REVIEW_OPEN_POS.text.en: Review open purchase orders for US-origin steel, appliances, agricultural equipment, paper and electronics.

actions.ACT_REVIEW_OPEN_POS.note.en: These are the named counter-tariff sectors. Decide deliberately whether to bring an order forward, hold it, or source elsewhere.

actions.ACT_CONFIRM_INCOTERMS.text.en: Confirm who pays the duty under your Incoterms on every live shipment in both directions.

actions.ACT_CONFIRM_INCOTERMS.note.en: This is the most common expensive surprise. The importer of record carries the liability regardless of who filed the paperwork.

actions.ACT_CHECK_YOUR_OWN_LINES.text.en: Check your own products against the published US list using the free CFIB tool or the Canada Tariff Finder.

actions.ACT_CHECK_YOUR_OWN_LINES.note.en: Both are free and both are better than anything this project would build. Use them rather than guessing at a classification.

actions.ACT_ASSEMBLE_EVIDENCE_PACK.text.en: Assemble the evidence pack that every support program will ask for, before any window opens.

actions.ACT_ASSEMBLE_EVIDENCE_PACK.note.en: Two years of financials, your US revenue concentration, affected headcount, and your top exposed inputs. Programs open on short notice.

actions.ACT_USE_A_BROKER_OR_RULING.text.en: Use a licensed customs broker for classification, or request a CBSA advance ruling for a binding answer.

actions.ACT_USE_A_BROKER_OR_RULING.note.en: No website, including this one, can classify your goods for you. The advance ruling is the only route that binds CBSA.

actions.ACT_LOCAL_TARIFF_HUBS.text.en: Start with Invest Brampton's tariff hub and Invest Mississauga's Partners in Trade.

actions.ACT_LOCAL_TARIFF_HUBS.note.en: Both are actively maintained, both aggregate the funding programs, and both give you an actual person to speak to locally.

actions.ACT_AUTO_AND_PARTS_IN_PEEL.text.en: If you are in auto or parts, note that motor vehicles are on the Section 338 list, contrary to a lot of early commentary.

actions.ACT_AUTO_AND_PARTS_IN_PEEL.note.en: This matters more in Peel and Windsor-Essex than anywhere else in the country.

actions.ACT_MAP_YOUR_AREA.text.en: Look up your own neighbourhood's exposure on the University of Toronto's mappingtariffs.org.

actions.ACT_MAP_YOUR_AREA.note.en: It maps business counts and employment exposure down to the dissemination area. Note that its underlying data predates the August 2026 escalation.

actions.ACT_WATCH_THE_GAZETTE.text.en: Canada Gazette Part II for the surtax order, then the CBSA customs notice that makes it operational.

actions.ACT_WATCH_THE_GAZETTE.note.en: Part II publishes every second Wednesday at 9am Eastern, with extra editions in a crisis. The customs notice is what brokers actually key.

actions.ACT_WATCH_DELIVERY_MECHANISM.tex.en: Whether the 25 billion dollar package arrives as new programs or as expansion of the existing BDC and regional agency channels.

actions.ACT_WATCH_DELIVERY_MECHANISM.not.en: The delivery mechanism determines how fast money actually reaches a firm, and it is the difference between weeks and quarters.

actions.ACT_WATCH_S338_CHALLENGE.text.en: Any court challenge to the first-ever use of Section 338.

actions.ACT_WATCH_S338_CHALLENGE.note.en: The statute has no judicial precedent. A successful challenge would unwind the 19 August measures entirely.

corrections[0].what.en: The counter-tariff and support-package records carried placeholder text ('Not yet published') that has now been filled in from primary sources, the steel and aluminum record now carries its scheduled increase to 50 percent, and all six shock records were re-checked against current sources as part of a scheduled review.

corrections[0].detail.en: Canada's counter-tariff product list and rate structure were published by Finance Canada on 25 August 2026 (updated 26 August): three rates of 15, 25 or 50 percent, each product matched to the rate the US charges on the equivalent Canadian good, covering 27.6 billion dollars of US imports. The federal support package record was updated to reflect the 7.5 billion dollars in new and enhanced measures Finance Canada announced 25 August 2026 (Regional Tariff Response Initiative, BDC Pivot to Grow, Canada Strong Diversification Fund, Rapid Response Supports for Workers and Employers, and expanded flexibility on the Large Enterprise Tariff Loan Facility), on top of the nearly 25 billion dollars in supports delivered over the prior 18 months. The steel and aluminum record was also updated: the same published list raises the rate on goods already covered by SOR/2025-95 from 25 to 50 percent effective 8 September 2026, under that order rather than a new instrument. The remaining three records (the US Section 338 tariffs, the wood cabinets safeguard, and the suspension of talks) were checked against current sources and found unchanged; only their verified dates were refreshed.

corrections[1].what.en: The safeguard on wood cabinets and vanities does not apply to goods from the United States or Mexico. This page previously said it applied regardless of origin.

corrections[1].detail.en: It said the charge applied "no matter which country they come from" and that it "applies regardless of origin". Checked against CBSA Customs Notice 26-17 and the Finance Canada announcement of 31 July 2026: goods originating in Canada, the United States, Mexico, Chile, Israel or another CIFTA beneficiary, and in developing countries, are outside the order. This mattered because a contractor pricing US-made or Mexican-made cabinets would have added a 25 percent line that does not exist. The record now states the exclusions, and that the measure is provisional for up to 200 days pending a Trade Tribunal inquiry due by 15 January 2027.

corrections[2].what.en: Two records that had never been checked against a primary instrument are now checked, and both carry sources.

corrections[2].detail.en: The steel and aluminum surtax is confirmed as SOR/2025-95, 25 percent of the value for duty on US-origin goods, in force since 13 March 2025 and last amended 1 September 2025 when Schedule 1 was replaced. The cabinets safeguard is confirmed and corrected as above. One limitation is now stated on the steel record rather than hidden: the consolidated text on the Justice Laws site is current only to 17 June 2026, so a more recent amendment would not appear there.

corrections[3].what.en: The page no longer loads webfonts from a third party.

corrections[3].detail.en: Three font families were being requested from Google Fonts on every page load, which disclosed each reader's address and user agent to a third party and contradicted the offline and nothing-collected claims this site makes. Removed. The page now makes no external request of any kind.
